title: E8 checking-order checkpoint form A
instructions: Composition checkpoint. The prompt asks how a skill you learned at school helped you somewhere else and what you learned. Your notes: you learned to divide a large task into owners and deadlines during a school exhibition; you used the method for a neighbourhood book swap; a checklist showed that nobody had arranged labels; you gave that job to someone before the event; you learned that when everyone can see who owns each job, a missing job is easier to spot and fix. You have eight minutes left to check your composition. You notice that you have not yet said what you learned, that your first sentence describes the colours of the book covers, and that one sentence has a verb that does not agree with its subject. Make all five decisions.

parts.prompt: Which check should you do first?

options.text: Add what you learned from using the method, since the prompt asks for it.
Change one repeated verb in the second paragraph to a different verb.
Fix the verb that does not agree with its subject.
Make the title of your composition one word shorter.

choice_rationales.A: The prompt requires the learning, so this is a missing part of the task.
choice_rationales.B: Word variety matters less than completing the task.
choice_rationales.C: Agreement belongs in the final sentence check.
choice_rationales.D: Title length does not complete the answer.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A missing part of the task must be fixed before any polishing.

parts.prompt: Which order of paragraphs gives the reader the clearest route?

options.text: Book colours → result → unrelated memory → method
Neighbourhood problem → school planning skill → book-swap use → missing job found and fixed → what I learned
What I learned → new event → book colours → result
Result → spelling check → school exhibition → a trip I took last year → a new claim about every event

choice_rationales.A: It starts with an unrelated detail and gives the result before its cause.
choice_rationales.B: Each paragraph prepares the reader for the next stage.
choice_rationales.C: The new event and the colours break the focus.
choice_rationales.D: A spelling check is not a paragraph, and the order is confusing.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The method should come before its result and the lesson learned.

parts.prompt: Which sentence should you remove because it does no useful job?

options.text: I gave each preparation job an owner and a deadline.
The checklist showed that nobody had arranged the labels.
Several donated novels had blue or green covers.
I gave the label job to someone before the event.

choice_rationales.A: This explains the method you used.
choice_rationales.B: This is evidence of what the method revealed.
choice_rationales.C: The cover colours do not help explain the method, result or lesson.
choice_rationales.D: This shows how you fixed the problem.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A detail should go if it does no job in answering the prompt.

parts.prompt: Which sentence about what you learned stays within your notes?

options.text: I learned that when everyone can see who owns each job, a missing job is easier to spot and fix.
I proved that every community event in the neighbourhood will succeed if it uses a checklist.
Exactly 99 per cent of organisers now prefer my system.
I learned that book swaps are always easy to organise.

choice_rationales.A: This matches what happened without claiming too much.
choice_rationales.B: One event cannot prove that every event will succeed.
choice_rationales.D: The notes do not show that every book swap is easy.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The lesson should go only as far as the actual result.

parts.prompt: After the task, order and content are secure, which check belongs in your last pass?

options.text: Turn your result into a stronger claim about every event.
Move the result back in front of the method.
Add another example that has nothing to do with the book swap.
Check that each verb agrees with its subject, for example ‘each job was’.

choice_rationales.A: This would make the content inaccurate.
choice_rationales.B: This would undo the order you fixed.
choice_rationales.D: Agreement is a sentence-level check for the final pass.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Once the meaning and order are secure, the writer checks agreement.
